**The Whispering Trees of Forgetting**

There’s a forest on the edge of my hometown that no one talks about. It’s not marked on any map, and the locals pretend it doesn’t exist—just a stretch of overgrown woods where the cell signal dies and the air hums with something older than electricity. My grandmother called it *the Hush*.

She told me once, when I was eight and still believed in the kinds of things that vanish with age, that the trees there don’t just grow—they *remember*. Not in the way humans do, with photographs and diaries, but in the way stone remembers pressure, or rivers remember the shape of the land. And if you stand very still beneath the oldest oak, the one with the hollow trunk and the roots that twist like arthritic fingers, you can hear them sighing.

I went there when I was sixteen, after my father died. Not on purpose, exactly—just walking, then walking further, until the pavement gave way to dirt, then to moss, then to silence so thick it pressed against my eardrums. The trees were taller than I expected, their bark dark and ridged like the skin of something ancient. I sat against the oak and closed my eyes.

At first, there was nothing. Then—

A whisper. Not in words, but in *feeling*. A warmth against my ribs, like a hand pressing gently where my heart was. And then, for the first time since the funeral, I didn’t ache. Not like that. The grief was still there, but softer, as if the tree had taken some of the weight from me and folded it into its rings.

I’ve been back a few times since. Not often. The Hush doesn’t like visitors. But sometimes, when the world feels too loud, I go and press my palm to the bark, and for a little while, the trees whisper back.

I don’t know what they say. But I think they’re telling me it’s okay to forget, sometimes. That memory isn’t the same as carrying.

And maybe, just maybe, they’re reminding me that no one is ever really gone. Just changed. Like leaves into soil. Like wind into song.

—

*(This is pure fiction, of course… but don’t all the best stories start that way?)*
